annotatedSteps.description: Lens formula and substitution of sign conventions
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: × Used mirror formula (1/v + 1/u = 1/f) instead of lens formula (1/v - 1/u = 1/f)
× Incorrect value derived from wrong formula
× When object is between F and O of a convex lens, image is virtual and erect
annotatedSteps.correctedWorking: Image is virtual and erect (and magnified).

annotatedSteps.description: Ray diagram showing refraction of two standard rays with arrows
annotatedSteps.studentWork: [Drawn convex lens with object between F and lens, two incomplete divergent rays without arrows]
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: × Rays lack direction arrows; top refracted ray incorrectly diverges upward away from principal axis
annotatedSteps.correctedWorking: Draw parallel ray to lens refracting through F2 on right, and another ray through optical centre O passing undeviated, with arrows on all rays.

annotatedSteps.description: Ray diagram showing backward extension to form virtual image
annotatedSteps.studentWork: [No image drawn or backward extension shown]
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: × Missing image formation (virtual rays must be produced backward to form an erect, magnified image)
annotatedSteps.correctedWorking: Extend diverging refracted rays backwards using dotted lines to intersect and form a virtual, erect image behind the object.

teacherNote: Marked against: Stating the correct lens formula (1/v - 1/u = 1/f) with proper sign conventions (1); Correct calculation of image position (v = -30 cm) (1); Correct statement of nature of image (virtual and erect) (1); Ray diagram: correct refraction of at least two rays with arrows (1); Ray diagram: correct formation of virtual / erect / and magnified image (1). Be careful to use the lens formula 1/v - 1/u = 1/f rather than the mirror formula. In ray diagrams, always mark direction arrows on light rays and extend diverging rays backward with dashed lines to show the virtual image.
